narrative:
The model determined that you have a 39% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses for approval, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only about 13% have a negative balance, while nearly 60% have no checking account at all. This situation pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Two other details worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. First, the 15-month duration you requested is noticeably shorter than the 19-month average among people who were approved. Second, the 1,721 DM you asked for is well below the typical 3,020 DM requested by approved borrowers. Both of these choices helped reduce the risk score.

Even with those positive elements, the negative signal from your checking-account status outweighed them. To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account back into positive territory before reapplying, or consider requesting a smaller, shorter-term loan once your balances improve. This single change is likely to have the largest impact on future decisions. (218 words)
